messages:
alex: Ran an end-to-end sweep comparing streaming (SSE/WebSocket) vs non-stream HTTP for the new 70B-q4 model across A100/H100/L4 in us-east1 / eu-west1 / ap-southeast1. Charts attached. TL;DR: SSE gives +10–25% peak throughput at equivalent p95 for short sequences; WS gives lower p50 under high concurrency. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

priya: Nice — can you paste the key numbers (p50/p95 RPS) per GPU/region?

alex: Quick select numbers from the sweep (seq_len avg 64 tokens, 512 max, batch policy = continuous batching for non-stream):
- us-east1 A100 non-stream: p50 42ms, p95 290ms, peak throughput 220 rps per GPU
- us-east1 A100 SSE: p50 48ms, p95 260ms, peak throughput 265 rps per GPU
- us-east1 H100 non-stream: p50 36ms, p95 210ms, peak throughput 350 rps
- us-east1 H100 SSE: p50 40ms, p95 190ms, peak throughput 420 rps
- eu-west1 L4 non-stream: p50 58ms, p95 460ms, peak throughput 95 rps
- eu-west1 L4 WS: p50 54ms, p95 430ms, peak throughput 115 rps
(These are single-GPU numbers with our default kernel selection and q4_0 quant.)

jamie: Were these runs with prefix/KV cache enabled and what was the batching window?

alex: Prefix cache = on (hot prefixes only). Non-stream batching: max_batch_size=64, max_latency_ms=30. Streaming uses continuous batching with soft batch flush at 20ms. Example config we used:
```
endpoint_mode: sse
batching:
  mode: continuous
  max_batch_size: 32
  max_latency_ms: 20
prefix_cache:
  enabled: true
  hot_threshold: 1000
```
And for non-stream:
```
endpoint_mode: http
batching:
  mode: flush_on_full
  max_batch_size: 64
  max_latency_ms: 30
```

sofia: Kernel choices matter — on H100 the matmul tiling picked by cuDNN variant X gave ~12% better throughput for SSE paths (smaller micro-batches) vs the fallback kernel used on A100. Also observed attention-kernel switch at seq_len ~128.

rafi: For live traffic I'd recommend soft-pin streaming routes to H100 in us-east1 and leave HTTP heavy batch jobs on A100s. Autoscaler policy: min_replicas=4 for streaming, burst_policy=scale_fast.

deploy-bot: Perf-CI: sweep-1937654321 completed. No functional regressions. Attached raw CSVs.

priya: What about quantization sensitivity? q4 -> q8 tradeoffs? Any quality regressions?

alex: q4_0 vs q8_0 quick notes: q4_0 reduces memory + increases throughput by ~20% on L4 but p95 latency unchanged; q8_0 gives +8–10% throughput vs q4 but with noticeable memory pressure on A100 for large batch sizes. On quality: small drop in greedy perplexity (~0.6%) for q4_0, no high-severity regressions on our eval set. We'll run full evals against the prompt-suite.

jamie: Can we reproduce with longer contexts (512/1024) and spikes of concurrent small requests (1–2 tokens) — that's where WS might shine. Also want kernel debug logs for H100 to see why tiling prefers that kernel.

alex: Agreed. Next steps I suggest:
1) Rerun critical cells with seq_len 256 and 1024 and with q4_0/q8_0 across GPUs in eu-west1 and ap-southeast1.
2) Enable kernel debug on two H100 replicas and collect matmul profile.
3) Load test WS with small payloads (1–3 tokens) at 10k concurrent connections to measure p50 p95 tails.
I'll schedule runs and post results. :+1:

sofia: Added to eng-ml drive: /perf/sweeps/1937654321/raw and summary. I put the chart PNGs in the folder.

rafi: I'll prototype a soft-routing rule for streaming: prefer H100 unless load > 85% then fall back to A100. Should be low-risk.

alex: Cool — thanks all. We'll reconvene after the longer-context runs. :rocket:
